Pay a monthly fee and get mystery bottles, so that you can skip the part where you stand in a shop squinting at labels and pretending you know what “structured” means. Or, if you’re like me, you buy wine based on what the label looks like alone. And some clubs deliver on that. Some of them, though, are just a subscription box with a wine cork glued to the lid. Videos by VICE So we asked sommeliers and wine-industry pros which clubs they’d actually recommend. Here are 12 of them, plus what the pros say separates a real club from a curated cash-grab scam. How to Actually Vet Wine Clubs While the pros all had their own specific picks below, there were a few things the pros all agreed on, regardless of which club they recommended. Price-check the per-bottle cost against what you’d spend on something similar at a restaurant, since you’re paying for the wine plus the research and delivery. Email a company a few questions before signing up. Thoughtful answers mean they care, generic ones mean keep looking. Flexibility is also a good sign. A club that locks you into shipments you don’t want is less of a perk, and more of a warning. If nobody involved can tell you who actually made the wine in your box, that’s the clearest red flag there is. You could have just as much luck blindly buying a mass-produced bottle of wine from your local corner liquor store. With those vetting strategies, you can be well-positioned to head off in search of the perfect wine club for you. Here are a few clubs to help kick off your search. Plonk Wine Club We’ll kick off this list with a VICE pick. Plonk Wine Club is an organic and biodynamic club curated by WSET and American Sommelier Association-certified founder Etty Klein, who specializes in hunting down indigenous grape varieties from under-the-radar regions like Croatia, Slovenia, Greece and Hungary. Choose red, white or mixed, in 4, 6 or 12-bottle shipments, with free shipping and detailed tasting notes plus recipe pairings included. (opens in a new window) Plonk Wine Club Plonk Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at Plonk Buy Now (opens in a new window) Parcelle Wine Drop Reynolds’ own company’s club, Parcelle Wine Drop offers three sommelier-picked bottles a month for $95, or $150 for a bigger pour, shipped nationwide from Parcelle’s NYC cellar. Full disclosure: this is Reynolds recommending his own product, named alongside King’s club. Personally, I‘m drawn to the artwork on the website… similar to how I select wines because of the label, I guess. (opens in a new window) Parcelle Wine Parcelle Wine Drop (opens in a new window) Available at Parcelle Wine Buy Now (opens in a new window) King’s Wine Club King’s Wine Club comes recommended by Grant Reynolds, sommelier and founder of NYC wine shop Parcelle, which helps fulfill this club for the Soho restaurant King. Reynolds says it consistently mixes “benchmark producers and new discoveries,” making a solid pick if you want a restaurant wine director’s palate without the reservation. (opens in a new window) King Wine King Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at King Wine Buy Now (opens in a new window) Primal Wine Club Primal Wine Club is a Los Angeles-based natural wine club shipping small-batch, biodynamic bottles from producers around the world, with a choice of mixed, red, white or orange selections. Recommended by Dylan Dinsmore, a WSET-2 certified sommelier and bar manager at FiNO in Denver, for drinkers who want global range without sacrificing low-intervention winemaking. (opens in a new window) Primal Wine Primal Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at Primal Wine Buy Now (opens in a new window) Orange Glou A New York club built entirely around skin-contact and pét-nat wines (which are naturally sparkling), Orange Glou was founded by sommelier Doreen Winkler. Also a Dinsmore pick, it’s a good option if you already know you like orange wine and want a curator who specializes in nothing else. (opens in a new window) Orange Glou Orange Glou Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at Orange Glou Buy Now (opens in a new window) Mondo Vino Dinsmore’s local pick is Mondo Vino —a Denver bottle shop’s in-house natural wine club, picking three hand-selected bottles a month curated by owner Duey Kratzer (Guild of Master Sommeliers). Worth knowing about if you want a club with a real storefront behind it, not just a warehouse. (opens in a new window) Mondo Vino Mondo Vino Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at Mondo Vino Buy Now (opens in a new window) The Good Sip Paige Comrie, WSET Level 3-certified wine educator behind Wine with Paige , also recommends her own quarterly club, and says so upfront: “I’m not going to pretend to be neutral about it.” The Good Sip club is built around small-production winemakers she can trace back to a real person, if that kind of production process is what appeals to you. (opens in a new window) The Good Sip The Good Sip Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at The Good Sip Buy Now (opens in a new window) The Set Wines The Set Wines is a Sta. Rita Hills club recommended by Katy Rogers, WSET-certified founding partner at wine marketing agency Likely Story Strategies (formerly 15 years at Jackson Family Wines). There’s no contracts or minimums with this one. Members choose bottle count and timing, earn points toward tastings and merch, and can taste directly with the winemaker on-site—great for if you’re local to the area! (opens in a new window) The Set Wines The Set Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at The Set Wines Buy Now (opens in a new window) Niner Wine Estates Another Rogers pick, based in Paso Robles, Niner Wine Estates offers customizable 4, 6 or 12-bottle shipments three times a year with free shipping, plus 20–25% off wine, food and merch at the winery’s on-site restaurant. Members also get access to a free, property-wide members-only week each year. (opens in a new window) Niner Wine Estates Niner Wine Estates Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at Niner Wine Estates Buy Now (opens in a new window) Austin Hope Winery Rogers’ third pick, and the one she frames less around club mechanics and more around treatment, is Austin Hope Winery . She says the Paso Robles winery trains staff (using the hospitality book Unreasonable Hospitality ) to add personal touches, like an extra bottle tied to something a member mentioned on a past visit. (opens in a new window) Austin Hope Winery Austin Hope Winery Wine Club (opens in a new window) Available at Austin Hope Winery Buy Now (opens in a new window) Madson Wines Madson Wines comes recommended by Kenneth Murray, sommelier at Pebble Beach Food & Wine and Director of Wine Programs at The Apis Hotel & Restaurant in Kenosha, WI. This Santa Cruz Mountains producer offers single-vineyard, often single-varietal bottlings, with some wines (like its Chenin Blanc and Aligoté) sold exclusively to club members. (opens in a new window) Madson Wines Madson Wines Club (opens in a new window) Available at Madson Wines Buy Now (opens in a new window) Champagne Happy Hour Murray’s most niche recommendation is Champagne Happy Hour —a husband-and-wife-run club sourcing exclusively from small grower-producers in Champagne. He calls it “a CSA box for bubbles,” and says it may be the best value in Champagne clubs specifically, if not wine clubs generally. https://americanbazaaronline.com/2026/08.text: Hunter Biden mocks Trump over secret catering truck exit Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Email Hunter Biden has aimed at President Donald Trump over his secret departure from Turkey last month, contrasting the episode with his father Joe Biden’s covert 2023 trip to Kyiv during Russia’s war in Ukraine. In a video circulating on social media, Hunter Biden praised his father’s decision to travel to Kyiv at age 80, describing the journey as a dangerous presidential trip into an active war zone. He then mocked Trump’s use of an airport catering truck to secretly leave Air Force One during a trip to Turkey. “My dad at 81 years old secretly got on a military aircraft, went to Ukraine, took a train for 16 hours to Kyiv as the first President of the United States to go into an active war zone. Donald Trump fits his fat ass into a food cart truck and brings his work wife with him instead of the guy that carries the nuclear codes,” Hunter Biden said. The remarks were shared by X user Reggie B. in a post that has drawn significant attention online. Multiple social media accounts have reposted the video and the comments. The comparison refers to two very different presidential security operations. READ: USCIS public charge rule takes effect September 18 (August 21, 2026) Joe Biden made an unannounced visit to Kyiv in February 2023, becoming the first sitting U.S. president to visit a war zone where American troops were not providing security. Biden secretly traveled aboard an Air Force C-32 to Poland before taking a roughly 10-hour overnight train journey into Kyiv. The trip had been planned for months and involved a tightly controlled group of White House, intelligence, military and Secret Service personnel. The United States also notified Russia about Biden’s travel shortly before his departure as a precaution against a potential military miscalculation. Trump’s 2026 operation involved a different security concern. According to The Washington Post, an Iranian assassination threat prompted an elaborate plan to move Trump secretly from Turkey to a smaller military aircraft. Trump had publicly appeared to board Air Force One after the NATO summit in Ankara, but he and several aides instead used an airport catering truck to move from the presidential aircraft to a C-32A. The operation was reportedly conducted without the knowledge of some White House staff and journalists who remained aboard the larger aircraft. The Washington Post reported that Trump was accompanied by several close aides, including Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino, executive assistant Natalie Harp and Oval Office operations director Walt Nauta. No Cabinet officials were on the catering truck, according to a U.S. official cited by the newspaper. ABC News separately reported that the unusual maneuver was part of an effort to conceal Trump’s flight from Turkey to the United Kingdom because of threats to his life. READ: Proposed H-1B fee rule clears White House review (August 20, 2026) Hunter Biden’s comments have turned the unusual security operation into a political comparison between the two presidents’ approaches to traveling under security threats. While Biden’s 2023 journey involved a lengthy covert trip by aircraft, motorcade and train into Kyiv, Trump’s 2026 departure involved a short transfer through an airport catering vehicle before he boarded another military aircraft. The contrasting episodes have since become fodder for political commentary online, with supporters and critics of both presidents debating what the two trips say about presidential leadership, security and public image. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/10/phil.text: A passenger ferry caught on fire overnight on Thursday off the western Philippines, killing at least five and leaving dozens of people missing.The blaze broke out on the M/V June Aster Wednesday evening about 2.2 km offshore, the Philippine Coast Guard said.The ferry had sailed from the capital Manila and was near its destination of Coron in Palawan province when the blaze broke out on Wednesday night.More than 40 people have been rescued, Coast Guard spokeswoman Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said, despite challenging weather conditions. Five casualties had been brought ashore."Based on the data we have right now on rescued (42) and the casualties, we still have 86 people who are unaccounted for," Cayabyab told a local radio station on Thursday.She said 134 people were on board, 117 of them passengers and 17 crew. No information was available about any foreigners on board."We are continuing search and rescue operations," she said, with a coast guard ship and high-speed response boats joined by a military vessel and other government boats, private volunteers and fishermen.Passengers were helped into smaller boats taking them to shallow water, and smoke still wafted over the charred vessel by midday on Thursday.The Philippine Coast Guard later told reporters that another person had been rescued, but their identity had yet to be confirmed."Just to make it clear, this is live data and may change as our search and rescue operations are ongoing," Cayabyab said in the radio interview."However, we have not yet been able to obtain information from the rescued individuals because we have not been able to speak with them," she said, adding that attempts to put out the blaze were ongoing.There were no immediate reports of foreigners on board.In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.The M/V Trisha Kerstin 3 sank along nearly the same route where 31 people died in 2023 after a fire broke out aboard the Lady Mary Joy 3 ferry.

https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/19/trum.text: US President Donald Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russian officials and key pillars of its economy on Friday, that is meant to punish and pressure Moscow for its ongoing war against Ukraine.The measure was a final legacy item for the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a close ally and friend of the president who had just returned from Ukraine when he unexpectedly died in July.In the works for more than a year, the bill passed with large bipartisan margins; 86-11 in the Senate and 262-159 in the House.It’s meant to starve Russian President Vladimir Putin of the resources Moscow needs to continue its war in Ukraine after invading its neighbour in February 2022.The bill, co-drafted by Senator Richard Blumenthal, sanctions Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers the Kremlin uses to evade existing Western sanctions and keep Russian energy moving.“I wish Lindsey were here to celebrate this historic day. I know he would be so proud. Lindsey believed this bill, which he worked on for well over a year, would help end the war through squeezing Putin economically and forcing his customers to re-evaluate their relationship with Russia,” said Senator Darline Graham, Lindsey Graham's sister, in a statement Friday.Darline Graham was appointed to complete her late brother's Senate term, set to end on the 3rd of January 2027.“If he were here today, he would be jubilant about our bill’s passage — and already thinking about the next one,” Blumenthal said of Graham after the House passed the legislation on Wednesday evening.“Putin is a thug who understands only force and strength, which is what we must show clearly and unequivocally,” Blumenthal added.The bill also enables Trump to impose up to 100% tariffs on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia’s natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.Despite overwhelming support on Capitol Hill, the legislation faced criticism from a vocal set of Democratic lawmakers, who favoured a tougher stance on Russia, but warned that Trump could use his new expanded tariff powers to impose fresh levies in the European Union and elsewhere.“Why in the world would this Congress or the People’s House give this president unfettered authority to visit more tariffs on the world that will have an adverse economic impact on the American people?” said Democrat lawmaker and House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries.Graham’s journey to getting Trump’s sign-off on the bill had been full of turbulence, as the White House had to be convinced that the president would be able to retain sufficient flexibility on sanctions.Eventually, Trump gave a final nod of approval to the bill after it included his push for a provision which would enable his administration to extend sanctions on Iran for another five-year period.

https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-parli.text: LUXEMBOURG — The European Parliament can’t review the secret ballot votes that blocked the far right from key positions, its lawyers told a court in Luxembourg today. In court, the Parliament’s lawyer, Niklas Görlitz, said: “The results of the vote are definitive. There’s no mechanism in our rules to redo the vote.” The EU’s General Court was hearing a case brought by the Patriots for Europe group, which is challenging the long-standing firewall set up by Europe’s centrist forces — the European People’s Party, the Socialists and Democrats, the liberals of Renew, and the Greens — to keep the far right away from decision-making. Advertisement Advertisement Specifically, the Patriots are contesting elections in which the chairs and vice-chairs of parliamentary committees were selected after the 2024 EU election. Those jobs were filled through voting in secret ballots. The group is also questioning the composition of the Parliament’s international delegations, saying its lawmakers were kept away from key roles. Lawyers for the Patriots — home of France’s National Rally, Spain’s Vox and Hungary’s Fidesz, among others — said its MEPs being kept from top committee jobs was a “categorical exclusion” and it was “not acceptable” for the Parliament’s third-largest party to be locked out of these positions. The Patriots have 85 lawmakers in the 720-strong chamber. Top jobs in Parliament come up for grabs again in January 2027, giving the Patriots another chance to try to get into powerful positions. Hungarian lawmaker Kinga Gál, the Patriots’ first vice-president, has previously called the mainstream parties’ actions “outrageous” and “against the rule of law.” The Patriots’ lawyer, Azelio Fulmini, referred to the EU institution’s own description of representation. “This proportional distribution of leadership positions within Parliament prevents the dominance of political life by just one or two large political groups, ensuring that smaller political groups also have a say in setting the political agenda,” he read. Advertisement Advertisement “I don’t know if there’s a clearer declaration than that,” he said, adding that he was reading directly “from the European Parliament’s website.” Görlitz told the court that all groups can nominate candidates for key jobs, adding: “Not getting the votes … doesn’t justify your tribunal getting involved in our affairs.” The Patriots’ lawyer accused the Parliament of going beyond the neutral administration of committee elections, arguing that officials helped implement a political agreement designed to keep the group out of leadership posts. EPP chief Manfred Weber told POLITICO in May 2025 that giving the far right access to executive posts was a red line. Over the past two years, his group has repeatedly passed legislation with the far right’s support. The presiding judge, the court’s new president Savvas Papasavvas, did not give a date for the court’s decision.

Photograph: Kent Nishimura/AFP/Getty Images Donald Trump Zelenskyy furious as Trump announces deal to buy Russian diesel President says deal essential to lower US fuel prices but move set to create fresh crisis with Ukraine and Nato allies US politics – live updates Robert Tait in Washington Fri 9 Oct 2026 19.39 EDT Last modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 20.07 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Donald Trump was on a fresh collision course with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and European allies on Friday after a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel, upending years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its four-and-a-half year war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy reacted furiously to Trump’s announcement of the deal with President Vladimir Putin of Russia, calling it “absolutely terrible” and “not fair and not honest”. In a move likely to create a fresh crisis with Washington’s Nato allies, Trump announced the deal with Putin on his Truth Social network, saying it was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared as a result of his decision to go to war with Iran. “I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, wherein it was agreed that Russia will immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace, another 500,000 Tons during the month of November, and 1,000,000 Tons immediately thereafter,” Trump wrote. “Based on the condition of their diesel refineries, Russia will then deliver, within a short period of time, 3,000,000 tons of diesel fuel.” He added: “Diesel prices for Americans and, indeed, the world, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST! Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my greatest priority.” Fuel prices have rocketed due to Iran’s closure of the strait of Hormuz, a strategically sensitive choke point that was the passageway for 20% of the global oil supplies before the war. While costs have risen for motorists – with a gallon of fuel now averaging $4.20 – it is the soaring price of diesel, which last month rose to a record high of $6.52, that has inflicted the most political damage to Trump and the Republicans as November’s midterm approach. Diesel is the main supply chain fuel, and a rise in its costs feeds into consumer prices and also hurts US farmers, who need to operate machinery. The agreement was criticized by Democrats, who said it undercut a law Trump signed last month allowing for a broad range of sanctions on Russian banks, officials and tankers, as well as directing him to impose steep tariffs on the top five importers of oil or natural gas from Russia. The law gave Trump wide discretion to make exceptions to its provisions. “This is what failure looks like. Failure for President Trump to live up to his promises to lower costs for Americans. Failure to protect America from its adversaries,” the Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, joined by Senator Jeanne Shaheen, who is the top Democrat on the Foreign Relations Committee, and Senator Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the Banking Committee, said in a statement. “Failure to follow the law and the bipartisan will of Congress that only weeks ago passed legislation aimed at cutting off revenue for Russia’s war machine and curbing purchases of Russian oil and gas.” Some Republicans were also critical of the agreement. “Propping up Putin’s war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities,” congressman Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican, wrote on X . “The President’s policies towards Russia and Ukraine are failures. We need moral clarity not moral ambiguity.” Perhaps the fiercest response came from Zelenskyy, who told Axios that it “looks like a happy birthday present for Putin. It looks absolutely terrible.” The Russian leader turned 74 earlier this week. In a long social media post, Zelenskyy, who has had an uneasy relationship with Trump, said the deal amounted to “an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged”. Russia was likely to repay it with “further terror and perfidy”. “It plays into Russia’s hands – allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said. Trump announced the oil deal as his envoys, Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, met with Ukrainian and European officials in Miami to discuss proposals to end the war. Zelenskyy, in a separate statement released by Ukraine’s embassy in Washington on Friday, said the Ukrainian negotiators had been “used as a smokescreen for the deal”, which he called “a weak decision by strong partners”. “That is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,” he said. Trump has recently criticized Ukraine for attacking Russian diesel refineries, calling on Zelenskyy to choose alternative targets. The Ukrainian leader rejected the request unless Russia accepted a reciprocal de-escalation plan that would stop Moscow attacking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. The agreement also comes on the heels of rising tensions between Russia and Washington’s Nato allies in Europe, amid speculation that Moscow might be preparing military action intended to test the alliance’s resolve. The latest development is likely to lead to a further deterioration of Zelenskyy’s relationship with the Trump administration. He was infamously ambushed by Trump and the vice-president, JD Vance, last year in an explosive White House encounter when the president told him: “You don’t have the cards.” But Trump has since reportedly grown disenchanted with Putin, expressing disappointment in his failure to reach a deal. Trump’s willingness to reach an agreement with Putin that will lower fuel costs comes despite Russia’s support for Iran in its war with the US. Russia is believed to have given Iran satellite intelligence and overhead surveillance data detailing the locations of American forces, ships, aircraft and military bases. It has also provided drone components and ammunition.
